newsitem.title: USA: MobileMedia, TCI mar quiet US corporate bond trade.
newsitem.headline: MobileMedia, TCI mar quiet US corporate bond trade.

text.p: U.S. corporate bond spreads were firm in typically light Monday trade, except for sharp losses in debt from TCI Communications Inc and MobileMedia Corp, dealers said.

Junk-rated MobileMedia's 9-3/8 percent debt traded off more than 10 basis points from Friday's close, traders said, following the company's announcement that it may default on about $11 million in November debt service.
MobileMedia's zero coupon debt also dropped 10 points to a 55 bid, 60 offer market.
Few bonds were said to trade despite the drop.

The company first said third quarter earnings could place it in violation of certain bank covenants in late September. The company on Monday said it is in talks with bank agents and is mulling whether it will make the coupon payments.

In other high-yield trade, Sinclair Broadcast Group debt was knocked one and a half points lower in response to news on Friday that it expects flat revenues and a four to five percent decline in third quarter cash flow.
The 10 percent 2005 debt closed at 98-1/2 bid, 99 offered.
Sinclair shares dropped nine points to 34-3/4, meanwhile.

Elsewhere, high-grades traders pushed TCI Communications' debt 15 basis points wider on average following a negative outlook by Standard & Poor's credit rating agency late on Friday. TCI debt due in 2000 widened to a 122 basis point bid, 111 offer compared with a 108, 105 market on Friday.
Bid-ask spreads for TCI debt widened more out the curve making for illiquid markets, traders said. TCI's 7-7/8s of 2026 were quoted at 275 bid, 247 offer, for example.
"You had reluctant sellers who aren't showing TCI's very cheap and then distressed buyers who were saying 'hit me,' so there wasn't a lot of commerce," one high-grades trader said.
Moody's Investors Service Inc cut TCI's senior unsecured debt to Ba1 from Baa3 on April 26.
Broadly speaking, secondary high-grade trading was quiet in all sectors with spreads quoted mostly flat, traders said.
In light new issuance, BankAmerica Corp issued $250 million A2/single-A rated subordinated notes due 2011 as 7.125s to yield 7.218 percent or 72 basis points over the Treasury curve.
Also, May Department Stores set $125 million 20-year A2/single-A rated debentures at par to yield 7.45 percent or 64 basis points over the Treasury long bond.

High-yield issuance was dormant on Monday but dealers and traders point to a rapidly mounting calendar. Supply comes in the face of suddenly negative mutual fund cash flows which have given the market a heavy tone, traders said.
High-yield traders focused on approximately 10 to 12 new issues in the next week or two. Expected issuance includes Australis Media, Poland Communications and Abraxas Petroleum.
In the governments market, prices marked time ahead of the Treasury's scheduled auctions of two- and five-year notes this week. The 30-year bond closed down 3/32 to yield 6.81 percent.
